featured_reviews.name: Gupta Rohit
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a nice place for fish/prawns buying. Market starts at 7 AM. You have to be tough negotiator here. Do not be in rush to buy, there are plenty of options, be careful while buying, there are chances you may be robbed of old fishes. You can get all the items chopped and cleaned, there are seperate people who cleans it up for you. I came across the cleaning chopping lady Gauri, if you are a noob in buying she can help you with good buy. If you have more time you can visit Bhau cha Dhakka but than it takes more to travel and you will have to be early bird and experienced to negotiate and have good find.

featured_reviews.name: Shishir Deshpande
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent for fresh sea food and sea food lovers who like cooking. A wide variety of fresh catch is available with fish like Pomphrets, Prawns / Shrimps, Crabs, lobsters et al.
The fresh catch comes every alternate day from the aversive jetty where the trawlers arrive every alternate days or so.
It’s a historical place in its own way.

featured_reviews.name: asif sharief shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good place for holesale fish in all variety

featured_reviews.name: Salim Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Fish market at Andheri west Versova. You need to have good bargain skills to buy anything from here. The sellers are quite humble and polite,  but also be ready to get insulted if you are trying to bargain at a very low price below the expected lowest price and when you irritate them. Don't get emotionally carried away with the stories the sellers might try to sell. They will never sell even at their cost price. And the term 'bony karo' will be heard a lot. Don't get carried away. They will never give away unless they make profits. Generally the fishes are quite fresh and good to eat. The quantity matters for a good deal.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a good place if you need to buy fish in large quantities. You will find fresh & good quality of Prawns, Surmai, Pomfret, Bangda & Bombayduck. Make sure to be there between 8AM to 9:30AM. Because after this time it is the small retailers who sell there. And if you want to get the fish cleaned : de-shelling the prawns, cleaning Bombayduck etc. you can get it done from small errand boys and girls who will do it for 30-50 Rs. Also be prepared to dare thru some fish slurry on the floor and ofcourse the STRONG  stench of fish.

featured_reviews.name: FROZZEN WORLD
featured_reviews.review_text: The connector of life... This place connects Versova Andheri to madh Island..... A short trip may be just a minute to cross the creek with ferry but saves almost two hours of your life. By road it's very hectic and full of traffic to reach madh Island and place across... You can take your bike also to cross.. it's usually full of bike and a que of bike from madh Island side to come to versova and vice versa..... Now they have made proper concrete plateform for commuters which is very convenient to enter and exit from ferry. Crossing alone may cost you Rs 5.00/- INR and Rs 20 to 40 with bike. I am waiting for the day when they arrange car transport also.

featured_reviews.name: Vinod Sivaraman
featured_reviews.review_text: Clean and functionally efficient. It is reasonably priced, payment is easy (cash or UPI), the place is accessible for able bodied persons. I didn't see any access for those who are unable to climb stairs. The frequency is good and the trip is safe enough in calm weather, zwith many life-jackets easily accessible. The water, though discolored, had no bad odour or any obvious or dangerous contaminants. A very positive experience, on the whole.

featured_reviews.name: Nidhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited the Versova Jetty and found it to be a very unique and important local travel spot. This jetty connects Versova to Madh Island (also known as Mud Island), which is home to the vibrant Koli fishing community and some beautiful residential areas.
What makes this place interesting is how it blends everyday life with a bit of Mumbai’s glamour. Many people, including residents from Madh Island and even celebrities like Archana Puran Singh and many other use this jetty to travel towards Andheri and Versova.
The ferry ride is very affordable (just around ₹10), making it a convenient option for daily commuters. However, it can get quite crowded, especially during peak hours, so be prepared for a bit of rush.
Overall, it’s not just a transport point but an experience of Mumbai’s local culture, community life, and coastal charm. Recommended for those who want to explore a different side of the city.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is an absolute mess during non monsoon times..locals over here have not taken efforts to keep this place clean.
The atmosphere over here is really polluted.
The water quality is extremely dirty. All the dirt and garbage from the sea is washed here.
Government is now taking efforts to clean this place.
Although this cons it is the right place to experience local fishermen lives. People who sail into the deep sea for a fresh catch, traditional boats,washed away boats are some of the attractionsover here. Ferry service is provided omto the other side of the boat for a cost of about ₹5.
If you are a person who wishes to research on local culture and livelihood then this may be the right place for you.
Hope you find it helpful.

featured_reviews.name: DNYANRAJ PATKAR
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the oldest fishing village in Mumbai city which was traditional village of Koli community. Small but colourful houses and narrow lanes are main features. featured_reviews.name: Rajib Saarkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Fish Market at Four Bunglow is one of the most authentic and vibrant seafood destinations in the city. If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a treasure trove. The market comes alive early in the morning with a wide variety of freshly caught fish, prawns, crabs, and even rare seasonal catches that you won’t easily find in supermarkets. The stalls are well-organized, and many vendors are friendly, knowledgeable, and willing to clean or cut the fish as per your requirement, which makes the whole experience convenient.

What stands out most is the freshness—there is a noticeable difference in taste compared to store-bought seafood. Prices are also quite reasonable, and with some bargaining, you can get excellent deals, especially if you’re buying in bulk. Regular customers often know which vendors offer the best catch of the day, so it’s worth exploring a bit before making your pick.

The market does get crowded during peak hours, especially weekends, but that adds to the bustling, energetic vibe. A pro tip is to go early in the morning to get the best selection. Since it’s a traditional fish market, be prepared for the typical sights, sounds, and smells, but that’s part of its charm and authenticity.

Overall, the Fish Market at Four Bunglow is not just a place to buy seafood—it’s an experience in itself. Freshness, variety, and local flavor all come together here, making it a must-visit for seafood enthusiasts.

featured_reviews.name: TravelWithDev04
featured_reviews.review_text:
Forget Juhu Beach. If you want the real Mumbai vibe, you need to head here.
Welcome to Versova Beach. Once a hidden spot, now it’s the ultimate escape for peace, cleaner sands, and the best community-led comeback story in the city.
It’s way less crowded than the tourist hubs. You’ve got the colorful Koli fishing boats on one side and some of the trendiest cafes in Mumbai just a lane away.
But the real reason people come? This sunset. Grab a coffee, find a spot on the rocks, and just watch the sky turn into a literal painting.
Pro Tip: Visit on a weekday for maximum peace. Tag your sunset partner in the comments and subscribe for more Mumbai gems!

featured_reviews.name: Vedant Anasune
featured_reviews.review_text: A very peaceful and refreshing beach that feels much more enjoyable now. It’s not as crowded as before, especially on weekdays, which makes it perfect for relaxing and spending quality time. The calm atmosphere, soothing sea breeze, and open space create really good vibes. It’s a great place to take a walk, sit quietly, or just unwind while watching the waves. The surroundings feel cleaner and more pleasant, making the overall experience even better. A perfect escape from the busy city life.

featured_reviews.name: Rajnand Thepade
featured_reviews.review_text: small and pleasant beach, perfect for a peaceful walk. It's usually cleaner compared to many other city beaches, making the experience nicer. You can also catch a ferry from nearby areas to Madh Island. The view of flights flying overhead during sunset is beautiful, and enjoying chana jor garam while watching the sunset makes it even better. A simple, relaxing spot in the city. You can also ride a horse.

featured_reviews.name: Rahmatullah Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Versova Beach is definitely one of the best beaches in Mumbai. You can have a great time here. A few years ago, it was full of trash and marine debris, but thanks to the efforts of Mr. Afroz Shah, this beach got a new lease on life.

This beach is very family-friendly and less crowded than Juhu Beach. Moreover, I have visited it several times myself and always enjoyed the experience.

If you are planning to visit this beach, I have one small request: please do not litter or throw garbage around. Let us all do our part to keep this beautiful place clean and tidy for everyone to enjoy.
